children: Artificial intelligence has become the dominant force in global venture capital, capturing more than three-quarters of venture dollars, while the exit market remained concentrated among a small group of large IPOs, according to HSBC.

AI and machine learning accounted for 77% of global venture deal value in the six months through June 30, up from 30% in 2023, while its share of deal count rose more modestly to 36% from 26%, analysts led by Shiva Joon said in an HSBC report. The gap showed that capital was increasingly flowing into a smaller number of much larger AI rounds.

The concentration was also visible in private-market valuations. HSBC found that AI companies commanded a premium over non-AI peers at every funding stage, with the gap widening sharply in later rounds. At Series D and beyond, the median AI company was valued at $4.25B compared with $644M for its non-AI counterpart, a 560% premium.

The IPO market, meanwhile, remained narrow despite signs that the exit window was beginning to reopen. Listings valued above $1B accounted for 82% of U.S. venture exit value in 2026, up from 4% in 2022, with HSBC noting that the recent mega-IPOs offered an indication that the window was opening but were not representative of the broader private market.

In 2026, IPO exit value was roughly 4.5 times private megadeal value, reversing a pattern from 2022 through 2025 when IPO exits were consistently smaller, and in most years only a fraction of private megadeal value. HSBC said the 2026 shift was driven almost entirely by the same three names.
Performance among the 10 most significant venture-backed listings of 2026 had been mixed. Four were trading below their offer prices, including Gemini Space Station
, meanwhile, were up 163% and 131%, respectively, according to HSBC.

HSBC's survey also found that investors remained more confident about private-market dealmaking than IPO activity, with 64% expecting VC and private-equity activity to increase over the next year, compared with 44% expecting IPO activity to rise. At the same time, 51% saw an AI capital-expenditure correction as a risk within six to 12 months.

title: AI captures 77% of global VC dollars as exits remain concentrated
